content:
ezra: Heads up — gpu-spot-us-west2 pool jumped to 0 Ready GPUs after the kernel rollout. Several nodes are Reporting "NotReady,NoSchedule" and the device-plugin never registers.

maria: ugh. logs? kubelet or device-plugin?

ezra: quick paste from one node:
```
$ kubectl -n kube-system logs nvidia-driver-daemon-abcde -c installer
ERROR: driver install failed: /var/lib/nvidia/driver-setup.lock held by pid 2345
+ apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
+ modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia not found in directory /lib/modules/5.10.0-xxxx
```
device-plugin shows: "failed to start gRPC server: listen unix:///var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins/nvidia.sock: bind: address already in use"

samir: maybe previous driver pod never cleaned up socket after CrashLoop -> kubelet thinks plugin is present -> nodes marked NoSchedule for nvidia.com/gpu resource.

jess: Any CSR approvals pending? Last time plugin created CSRs for node feature discovery.

infra-oncall: checked: 4 CSRs from "system:node-problem-detector" and none from device-plugin. Controller-manager looks healthy. I see a lot of `kubelet` warnings about stale device plugin: "rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed"

maria: Action plan: 1) cordon pool, 2) drain non-critical pods, 3) restart kubelet on one node to force socket cleanup, 4) roll driver DaemonSet image with backoff fixes.

ezra: I'll cordon/drain one node now and try kubelet restart on it. If it recovers, we can do a rolling fix. @infra-oncall please watch autoscaler — don't want it to scale down healthy nodes while we debug.

k8s-deploy-bot: Deploy triggered by @ezra: rolling-restart nvidia-driver-daemonset (image: nv/driver:535-fix1)

samir: After restart, /var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins/ had leftover nvidia.sock.old and a stale pid file. Removed both and restarted kubelet -> device-plugin came up and registered GPUs.

maria: Good sign. But pool had 6 preemptible nodes; autoscaler already started replacing drained ones with new nodes that lack the patched image -> those new nodes went NotReady faster.

jess: We should freeze autoscaler for this pool until the rollout completes, or make a temp launch template that includes the fixed image. Cost impact if we pause autoscaler? small for 20m.

infra-oncall: Paused cluster-autoscaler for nodepool/gpu-spot-us-west2 (reason: driver rollout). Will resume after 30m or manual resume.

ezra: Next steps: create DaemonSet image with init script that waits for module dir and cleans stale sockets: add retry loop + exponential backoff. Also add a preflight check in node bootstrap to ensure kernel modules exist before joining.

maria: I'll file a postmortem and include metric: node boot-to-ready went from 3m -> 12m, cost bump from extra spot churn ~ +$120 over the hour.

samir: For now, manual recovery worked. Plan to deploy patched DS to all zones, then unpause autoscaler.

jess: Thanks all. Please add runbook note for "stale device-plugin socket" (how to identify and remediate) and tag oncall-shift for docs update.

ezra: marking thread resolved once autoscaler resumes and 100% pool Ready. :white_check_mark:
